αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὸν: αὐτός — self; masc. acc. sg.: ’him(self)’ · also reinforcing σε: ’you yourself’ (σ’ αὐτὸν) · also acc. sg. reinforcing an unexpressed 1st-person pronoun: ’me myself’ (αὐτὸν δ’ ἐνθάδ’ ἔχουσα ’keeping me myself here’) · also plain acc. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, after a preposition: ἀμφ’ αὐτὸν ’around him’ · also plain acc. sg. pronoun of a thing, unemphatic ’it’ (masc. χιτών), as direct object of a verb: ἐθηήσαντο αὐτὸν ’gazed at it’ · also plain acc. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, direct object of a verb: θεὸς αὐτὸν ἐνείκαι ’a god might bring him’
αὐτὸς: αὐτός — self; masc. nom. sg.: ’himself’ · also masc. nom. sg. with a 1st-person subject: ’myself’ (ἐγὼν αὐτός) · also masc. nom. sg. with a 2nd-person subject: ’yourself’ (εἰδήσεις δὲ καὶ αὐτός ’you will see for yourself’) · also masc. nom. sg., of a thing: ’it itself’ (αὐτὸς … σίδηρος ’iron of itself’)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
αὖτις: αὖτις — back, again, once more; adv. (= αὖθις)
βάλεν: βάλλω — throw, cast; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, in tmesis with ἀμφί: ’threw about’ · also in tmesis with ἐπί (βάλεν δ’ ἐπὶ ... ἑκάστῳ = ἐπέβαλε): ’threw over, cast upon’ · also in tmesis with παρά (πάρ … βάλεν = παρέβαλε): ’threw beside, set before’ · also without tmesis, with κε, unreal past: ’would have hurled’ (κε … βάλεν … ποτὶ πέτρας ’would have dashed her against the rocks’) · also in tmesis with ἐν (ἐν … βάλεν = ἐνέβαλε): ’cast into, sent upon’ (φύζαν … βάλεν ’sent panic upon’) · also plain aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, with no tmesis: ’let fall’ (δάκρυ χαμαὶ βάλεν ’let a tear fall to the ground’) · also plain aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, ’hit, struck’, the target or the weapon given: σκοπὸν … βάλεν ’hit a mark’, βάλεν ἰῷ ’struck with an arrow’
βῆ: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη): ’went, strode’
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γένηται: γίγνομαι — come to be, happen; aor. subj. 3 sg., in a temporal clause with ἄν/κε: ’shall come’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a direct question of doubt/deliberation, no ἄν/κε: τί … γένηται; ’what is to happen?’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg., prospective in a negative statement with a relative clause: οὐδὲ γένηται ’nor ever shall there be’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a general relative clause without ἄν/κε: ’whatever shall come to pass’ (ὅσσα γένηται) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a fear clause after μή: ’lest it become’ (μή … ἕλωρ … γένηται ’lest it become prey’) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in an indirect clause after ὅπως: ’(consider) how it may turn out’ (ὅπως ὄχ’ ἄριστα γένηται) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. with κε, in a conditional or relative clause: ’shall prove, become’ (ὁππότερος … κε νικήσῃ κρείσσων τε γένηται; αἴ κέν … γένηται)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γυναικῶν: γυνή — woman; fem. gen. pl., partitive with δῖα: ’heavenly-one of women’ · also partitive with ἀρίστη: ’best of women’ · also possessive gen. with a noun: ἔργα γυναικῶν ’the works of women’ · also gen. after a verb of surpassing, ’above, beyond women’ (περίεσσι γυναικῶν) · also gen. pl. dependent on a noun of speech, ’of … women’ (φάτιν ἀνδρῶν ἠδὲ γυναικῶν ’the talk of men and of women’) · also fem. gen. pl., partitive with indefinite τις: ’one of the women’ (τις … γυναικῶν) · also fem. gen. pl. in apposition with δμῳάων: ’women (servants)’ (γυναικῶν δμῳάων ’women servants’)
γυναῖκες: γυνή — woman; fem. nom. pl., in apposition to δμωαί: ’women’ · also fem. nom. pl. in a pair: ’women’ (ἀνέρες ἠδὲ γυναῖκες ’men and women’) · also fem. nom. pl., plain subject: ’the women’ (of a household)
δέδαεν: δάω — teach (learn in the aor. pass.); reduplicated aor. 3 sg. act., epic (= Attic ἐδίδαξε), + double acc.: ’taught (the craft)’
δέμας: δέμας — bodily form, frame; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect: ’in body’ · also neut. acc. sg., direct object or in apposition: ’body’ (εἶδός τε δέμας τε ’form and body’)
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δήμῳ: δῆμος — district, land, people; dat. sg.
δαιμονίη: δαιμόνιος — strange, baffling, ill-starred; fem. voc. sg., epic -η (= Attic -α), reproachful address: ’strange one’
δαιμόνι: δαιμόνιος — strange, puzzling, odd (a voc. of address; the force, gentle or chiding, is uncertain); masc. voc. sg., elided (δαιμόνι’ = δαιμόνιε)
διαμπερές: διαμπερές — right through, clean through; adv.
δμῳὰς: δμῳή — female slave, servant-woman; fem. acc. pl., epic (cf. Attic δούλη)
δοκεῖ: δοκέω — seem, think; pres. 3 sg.: ’he seems’
δολιχηρέτμοιο: δολιχήρετμος — long-oared; fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), of a ship (νηός), two-ending adjective
δύναμίς: δύναμις — power, strength, ability; fem. nom. sg.
δύναμαι: δύναμαι — be able, can; pres. 1 sg.
δώματ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώματ’ = δώματα) · also neut. nom. pl., subject: κλυτὰ δώματ’ ἔασιν ’his famous halls are’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb: ’the house’
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’ · also with opt., in a wish: ’if only’ (εἰ … ὁμοφρονέοις … γένοιο) · also ὡς εἰ + opt., ’as if’ (ὡς εἰ … ἱκοίατο ’as if they had come’) · also ὡς εἰ, ’as if’, before a noun with no verb of its own (ὡς εἰ κέρα … ἠὲ σίδηρος ’as if horn or iron’)
εἰν: ἐν (epic εἰν before a vowel) — in, on; + dat.
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’) · also in the idiom εἰς ὅ (κε) ’until’: εἰς ὅ κεν … μιγήῃς ’until you mingle with’ · also in the idiom εἰς ὅτε (κε) + subj., ’until the time when’ (εἰς ὅτε κέν … καθέλῃσι ’until … brings down’)
εἰσιδέειν: εἰσοράω — look at, behold; aor. inf. (stem εἰσιδ-), epic uncontracted (= Attic εἰσιδεῖν): ’to look upon’
εἴπεσκε: εἶπον (aor. of λέγω/φημί) — say, speak; iterative impf. 3 sg. with suffix -σκε, epic (= ἔλεγεν ἄν): ’would say, used to say’
εἴρυσθαι: εἴρυμαι (= ἐρύομαι) — guard, protect, watch over; pres. inf.
εἵλετο: αἱρέω — take, seize; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’took up (for herself)’ · also with ἐκ in tmesis: ’took away from’ (ἐκ … εἵλετο)
εἵμαθ: εἷμα — garment, clothing; neut. acc. pl., aspirated and elided (εἵματα → εἵμαθ’ before rough breathing)
εἵματα: εἷμα — garment, clothing; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl., subject: εἵματα γάρ ῥ’ ἐβάρυνε ’for the clothes weighed him down’
εἷμαι: ἕννυμι — clothe, put on; perf. mid./pass. 1 sg., epic, with pres. force: ’I am clothed in, I wear’
εὐνήν: εὐνή — bed, bedding, marriage-bed; fem. acc. sg. · also of an animal’s lair, den (ἑὴν εἰσήλυθεν εὐνήν ’came into his own lair’, of the lion in the simile)
εὐρυνόμη: Εὐρυνόμη — Eurynome, the housekeeper of Odysseus’s house; fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg., in address: ’Eurynome!’
εὐρύκλεια: Εὐρύκλεια — Eurycleia, Odysseus’s old nurse; nom. sg.
εὐρὺ: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’widely’ · also attributive, agreeing with a neut. noun: ’wide’ (κλέος εὐρύ ’wide fame’)
ηὔδα: αὐδάω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., augmented (αὐ- → ηὐ-)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle · also with the relative ὅθι, no connective force: ὅθι θ’ ’where’ · also epic τε after a relative, no connective force (οὕς θ’ ’which’)
θαλάμου: θάλαμος — chamber, room; masc. gen. sg.
θεῖος: θεῖος — divine, god-inspired; masc. nom. sg.
θηλυτεράων: θηλύτερος — female, of womankind (epic comparative form of θῆλυς); fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
θρόνου: θρόνος — chair, seat; masc. gen. sg.
θυμός: θυμός — heart, spirit; masc. nom. sg. · also life, the breath of life
θυμὸν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg. · also the life that leaves the body: ’life’ (μελιηδέα θυμὸν ἀπηύρα ’took away (my) honey-sweet life’)
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὃς δέ κ’ … ἵκηται ’whoever comes’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κ’ ἐλθὼν … εἴποιμι ’and I would go and tell’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καί νύ κ’ … ἔδυ ’and … would have set’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’will’ (τοὺς δέ κ’ … θέλξει ’and then … will enchant them’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ μέν κ’ αἰνήσωσι ’if they approve’) · also + opt. in the protasis after εἴ: ’if perhaps’ (τόν κ’ εἴ μοι δοίης ’if you would give me him’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κ’ αὐτὸν γνώω ’if I come to know him’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κ’ … ἐρεθίζω ’so that I may provoke’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὥς: ’so that’ (ὥς κ’ … ἵκηται ’so that he may reach’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if you should wish’ (αἴ κ’ ἐθέλῃσθα)
κάρητος: κάρη — head; neut. gen. sg., epic κάρητος (= Attic κεφαλῆς)
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κέ τοι λύσῃ ’so that she may free’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κέ ποθι Ζεὺς δώῃ ’if Zeus should somehow grant’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἴ: ’if perhaps’ (εἴ κέ τιν’ … εὕρωμεν ’if we should find any’) · also + opt. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κέ μοι … παρασταίης ’if you would stand by me’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: τῷ κέ με … ὤνησεν ’would have benefited me’ · also + fut./short-vowel aor. subj. in a main clause: κέ τοι καταλέξω ’I shall tell you’ · also + opt. in the protasis after εἴ: ’if perhaps’ (εἴ κέ μιν ἀγγείλαιμι ’if I might report him’) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κέ τοι φήνωσι ’until they show you’) · also + subj. in a prospective relative clause: ’who shall’ (ὅς κέ με κεῖσ’ ἀγάγῃ ’who shall lead me there’) · also + fut. indic. (or short-vowel subj.) in a clause after εἴ: ’whether perhaps’ (εἴ κέ σφι … τελευτήσει ’whether … it will come to pass for them’) · also + opt., potential, in a main clause: ’might’ (καί κέ τεο … πειρηθεῖμεν ’we might test any of’) · also + impf. indic., unreal past: ‘would have been’ (καί κέ τοι … ἀμφεπονεῖτο ‘would have been busy for you’) · also + opt. in a relative clause: ‘from where you would’ (ὅθεν κέ τοι … ἄλφοι)
κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · also + aor. indic., unreal past: κέν μοι … κατέχευας ’you would have poured on me’ · also + subj. in a main clause: ’may’ (καί κέν οἱ ὑπέρσχῃ χεῖρα ’and he may hold his hand over him’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (κέν μοι … εἴη ’would be mine’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κέν τις … ὀρέξῃ ’if perhaps someone holds out’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κέν … μεταλλῶσιν ’whenever they ask’) · also + opt., potential, in a clause with ὅ ’that’: ’might’ (ὅ κέν τις … ἀμύνοι ’that someone might defend’)
κέρδος: κέρδος — gain, profit, advantage; neut. nom. sg.
κακὰ: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl., subject: κακὰ ἔργα ’bad deeds’
καλὸν: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; masc. acc. sg. (agreeing with a noun) · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’beautifully’ (with an infinitive) · also neut. acc. sg. used as a noun, direct object: ’a fine one’ (μάλα καλὸν ἑλών) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive, agreeing with a stated neut. noun: ’fine’ (καλὸν δέπας ’the fine cup’) · also neut. nom. sg., agreeing with ὕδωρ: ’fair, fine’ (ὕδωρ καλὸν ’fair water’) · also neut. acc. sg., adverbial or cognate with a finite verb: οὐ καλὸν ἔειπες ’you have not spoken well’ · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: ’a fine thing (to hear)’
κατ: κατά (elided κατ’) — down from, throughout; + gen./acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (κατ’ … ἕζετο = κατέζετο ’sat down’) · also + acc., of place, ’along’ (κατ’ ἠερόεντα κέλευθα ’along the misty paths’) · also + acc., ‘over against’ (κατ’ ἄντηστιν ‘right opposite’)
καταθνητῶν: καταθνητός — mortal, subject to death; masc. gen. pl. (καταθνητῶν ἀνθρώπων ’of mortal men’), epic by-form of θνητός
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’) · also + gen., ’down from’ (κατὰ πετράων ’down from the rocks’) · also + gen., ’all over, throughout’ (κατὰ σπείους κέχυτο ’lay spread all over the cave’) · also + acc., of the part grasped: ’by’ (κατὰ νῶτα λαβών ’taking him by the back’) · also + acc., ’on account of, on the business of’ (κατὰ χρέος ’on business’) · also + gen., ’down in, within’ (κατὰ σπείους κοίλοιο δέδυκεν ’is sunk in the hollow cave’) · also + acc., of the place struck: ’in, on’ (κατὰ δεξιὸν ὦμον ’on the right shoulder’)
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … ἐποτρύνῃ ’until … urges on’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κε πίῃ) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever, as soon as’ (ὅτε … κε θάνῃσιν; ἐπεί κε … λίπῃ) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κε … ἀκούσῃς) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κε λίσσηαι ’but if you beg’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καὶ νύ κε … βάλεν ’and she would have hurled’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κε θάνωμεν ’either we may die’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κε … μαχοίμην ’I would fight’) · also + subj. in a relative clause of purpose: ’who are to’ (οἵ κε … ἀγγείλωσι ’who are to announce’) · also + fut. indic. (or short-vowel subj.) in a main clause: ’will’ (αἶψά κε … ἀποτίσεται ’at once he will exact payment’) · also + aor. in a general relative clause: ’who would (decide)’ (οἵ κε … ἔκριναν) · also + opt. in a relative clause: ’whoever might’ (ὅς κε … πόροι ’whoever might offer’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κε … ἐντανύσῃς)
κεδνὰ: κεδνός — careful, trusty; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially with ἰδυῖα: ’trusty, knowing in her heart’
κεφαλῇ: κεφαλή — head; fem. dat. sg. · also periphrasis for the person: ’Achilles himself’ (Ἀχιλλῆος κεφαλῇ, dative of the person grieved for)
κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown, report; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. (same form), direct object: μέγα κλέος ἤρατο ’won great fame’; κλέος φέρειν ’bring report’
κλύον: κλύω — hear, hearken; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’they heard’
κουριδίοιο: κουρίδιος — wedded, lawful (of a spouse); masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), agreeing with φίλοιο: ’wedded’
κούρων: κοῦρος — boy, youth, young man; masc. gen. pl., partitive after ἄριστος: ’of the young men’
κραδίη: κραδίη — heart; fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg. (same form): ’heart!’ (τέτλαθι δή, κραδίη ’endure now, heart’)
κόμας: κόμη — hair, locks; fem. acc. pl.
κώεα: κῶας — fleece, sheepskin; neut. acc. pl. κώεα, epic uncontracted (the sg. is κῶας; prose says κῴδιον)
κὰδ: κατά (apocope κάδ before δ-) — down through, throughout; prep./preverb in tmesis: ’throughout the halls’ (κὰδ δώματα = κατὰ δώματα) · also a bare preverb in tmesis with a verb: κὰδ ... ἔβαλε = κατέβαλε ’threw down’
κὰκ: κατά (apocope κὰκ before κ-) — down; prep. + gen., ’down from’ (κὰκ κεφαλῆς) · also preverb in tmesis (κὰκ … εἴρυσσε = κατεῖρυσε ’drew down’)
κῆρ: κῆρ — heart; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect (φίλον κῆρ ’in his own heart’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a verb: κῆρ ἤθελε ’my heart wished’ · also κήρ — death-fate, doom; fem. acc. sg., elided (κῆρ’ = κῆρα): ’death-fate’ (θάνατον καὶ κῆρ’ ’death and doom’) · also neut. acc. sg., after ἀμφί: ’around the heart’
λέξομαι: λέγω (II) — lay down; mid. lie down, go to bed; fut. 1 sg. mid.: ’I will lie down’
λέχος: λέχος — bed, couch; neut. nom./acc. sg.
λίγειαν: λιγύς — clear-sounding, piercing, shrill; fem. acc. sg., epic accent (= λιγεῖαν)
λίην: λίαν — very much, exceedingly; adv., Ionic λίην (= Attic λίαν)
λίθοιο: λίθος — stone; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
λούσαντο: λούω — wash, bathe; aor. mid. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’washed themselves’
λοῦσεν: λούω — bathe, wash; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented: ’bathed’
λώϊον: λώϊος (comparative λωΐων) — better, more desirable (= Attic βέλτιον); neut. acc. sg., used as a noun: ’something better’
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγ: μέγας — great; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, elided (μέγ’ = μέγα): ’greatly’ · also plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. noun, not adverbial: κῦμα μέγ’ ’a great wave’
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’) · also μένω — stay, wait; pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (μέν’ = μένε): ’stay’
μαῖα: μαῖα — good mother, nurse; fem. voc. sg.: ’nurse!’, a respectful address to an older woman
μείζονά: μέγας — great, big; comparative μείζων, masc. acc. sg.: ’bigger, taller’
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μεγαλήτορα: μεγαλήτωρ — great-spirited, great-hearted; masc. acc. sg. (of Odysseus) · also of θυμός, ’great-hearted’ (μεγαλήτορα θυμόν)
μεταλλᾷς: μεταλλάω — inquire after, ask about; pres. 2 sg.
μητέρ: μήτηρ — mother; acc. sg., elided (μητέρ’ = μητέρα)
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μογήσας: μογέω — toil, suffer hardship; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having suffered’
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’) · also dat. of possession with εἰμί: ’who are mine’ (οἵ μοι ἔασιν ’who are mine’)
μολπῆς: μολπή — song, dance, music; fem. gen. sg.
μύθοισιν: μῦθος — word, speech; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’ · also negating a generic relative clause with the opt.: ὃς μὴ … ἐλάσειε ’whoever did not drive off’ · also ’lest’ in a warning, + 2 sg. fut./subj.: μὴ … ἀποτίσεαι ’lest you pay for it’ · also + inf., negating an infinitive of advice that gives the content of a word: ’not to’ (ἔπος … μὴ πάντα μνηστῆρσιν ὁμιλεῖν ’a word, not to mingle in everything with the suitors’)
μῆτιν: μῆτις — cunning intelligence, craft, counsel; fem. acc. sg.
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’)
νηὸς: ναῦς — ship; gen. sg., epic νηός (= Attic νεώς)
νῶϊ: ἐγώ — I; pron., 1st pers. dual nom. ’we two’, epic (= Attic νώ) · also dual acc.: ’us two’ (τις νῶϊ τίει ’someone honours us two’)
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’) · also encl. dat. sg. of a thing, ’to/for it’ (δύω δέ τέ οἱ θύραι ’and it has two doors’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’those, the’ (οἱ πέπλοι ’the robes’) · also dat. sg. of the giver with δέχομαι: ’from him’ (οἱ ἐδέξατο ’took from him’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἶδ: οἶδα — know; perf. 1 sg., elided (οἶδ’ = οἶδα) · also perf. 3 sg. (identical elided form): ’he/she knows’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ(ε) ’who knows’)
οἶκον: οἶκος — house, household (and its stores); acc. sg.
οἷος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg. · rough-breathed οἷος is relative ’such as, of the kind that’ (οἷος Ὀδυσσεὺς ἔσκεν ’such as Odysseus was’) · also οἷος in an indirect exclamation, ’what sort of’ (οἷος κείνου θυμός ’what sort his spirit is’)
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔλας: οὖλος — thick, woolly, curly; fem. acc. pl.
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὕτω: οὕτω(ς) — thus, so, in this way; adv.
οὗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. gen. sg.: ’whose’ (= Attic οὗ) · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐξ οὗ ’since, from the time when’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own; masc. gen. sg. agreeing with a noun (οὗ πατρὸς ’her own father’s’)
πάρεστιν: πάρειμι — be present, be at hand (παρά + εἰμί); pres. 3 sg., ν-movable
πάσσονα: παχύς — thick, stout; epic comparative πάσσων (= Attic παχύτερος), masc. acc. sg.: ’stouter’
πάτερ: πατήρ — father; voc. sg. · also πατέρα, masc. acc. sg., elided (πάτερ’ = πατέρα): ’father’ (μητρὸς … πάτερ’ ’mother’s father’)
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, title of Athena of unknown origin (perhaps πάλλω ’brandish’); nom. sg.
παντοίην: παντοῖος — of every kind, all sorts of; fem. acc. sg.
παρ: παρά (elided παρ’) — beside, among; + dat. · also + gen., ’from, from the side of’ (παρ’ Ἴλου ’from Ilus’) · also + acc., of motion, ’past, along, beside’ (παρ’ Μίμαντα ’past Mimas’)
πατρίδα: πατρίς — native land, fatherland; fem. acc. sg. (φίλην ... πατρίδα γαῖαν ’his dear fatherland’)
πειράζειν: πειράζω — try, test; pres. inf., by-form of πειράω (Attic πειρᾶν), + gen. or acc. of the person tried
πεπνυμένος: πέπνυμαι — have one’s wits about one, be prudent; perf. part. masc. nom. sg. (trad. linked to πνέω ’breathe’, though uncertain), stock epithet: ’prudent’
περί: περί — around, about; adv. ’exceedingly, beyond others’ (περί τοι μένος ’you have strength beyond others’) · also adv. or preverb with ἦλθε (περί … ἦλθε ’came about’), exact force uncertain · also prep. + gen., ’about, concerning’ (περί τ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ πάντων ’about himself and about all’) · also prep. + gen., ’for’, of what is at stake in a fight (περὶ ψυχέων ἐμάχοντο ’fought for their lives’)
περίφρων: περίφρων — circumspect, of sound understanding; fem. nom. sg., stock epithet of Penelope · also epithet of Arete: fem. nom. sg., ’the circumspect queen’ · also epithet of Eurycleia: fem. nom. sg., ’circumspect Eurycleia’
περιναιετάουσι: περιναιετάω — dwell around, live in the neighbourhood; pres. 3 pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic -ῶσι)
περιχεύεται: περιχέω — pour around, overlay; pres. mid. 3 sg., + acc. and dat.: ’overlays (gold) on (silver)’
πηνελόπεια: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope, wife of Odysseus; nom. sg.
πολλοὶ: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. pl.
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
πολυδένδρεον: πολυδένδρεος — many-treed, full of trees; masc. acc. sg., agreeing with κῆπον
πολυμνήστην: πολύμνηστος — much-wooed, with many suitors; fem. acc. sg.
πολύμητις: πολύμητις — of many wiles, epithet of Odysseus (built on μῆτις ’cunning intelligence’); masc. nom. sg.
πολύτλας: πολύτλας — much-enduring; adj., masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Odysseus (πολύ ’much’ + root of τλῆναι ’endure’)
πολὺ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’by far’ · also neut. nom. sg. adj. agreeing with ὕδωρ: ’much, plentiful’ · also neut. acc. sg. adverbial with a negative: ’far’ (οὐ πολὺ ναῖεν ’did not live far off’)
ποσσὶν: πούς — foot; masc. dat. pl., epic double σ (= Attic ποσί)
πρίν: πρίν — before, until; conj./adv., + inf. (like Attic πρίν) · also + a temporal clause (πρίν γ’ ὅτ’ ἄν + subj.): ’until the time when’ · also πρίν κε + opt., an independent potential clause answering a suppressed protasis: ’sooner, before then’ (πρίν κεν ... ἵκοιο ’you would arrive home before then’) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article, no inf.: ’formerly, at first’ (parallel to the by-form πρὶν) · also πρίν γ’ ὅτε + aor. indic.: ’until the time when’ (a definite past terminus) · also πρίν γε + subj.: ’until’ (πρίν γ’ ἔτι … πειρήσεαι ’until you have tried’)
προλιπὼν: προλείπω — leave behind, abandon; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.
προσέειπε: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
προσεφώνεε: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg., augmented (προσ- + ἐ-φώνεε): ’was speaking to, addressed’
προσηύδα: προσαυδάω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg.
πρόσθε: πρόσθε — before, in front; adv. · also prep. + gen.: ’in front of’ (πρόσθε ποδῶν ’before his feet’)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’ · also + gen., ’in the eyes of, with’ (πρὸς πόσιός τε καὶ υἱέος ’in the eyes of her husband and son’)
πρῶτα: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’first’
πτερόεντα: πτερόεις — winged (πτερόν ’feather, wing’); neut. acc. pl.: ’winged (words)’
πυκινὸν: πυκινός — thick, close-set, solid; masc. acc. sg.: ’solid’
πω: πω — yet, up to now; enclitic adv., usu. with a negative
πόληος: πόλις — city; gen. sg., epic (= Attic πόλεως)
πόσιος: πόσις — drinking; gen. sg. (abstract noun, distinct from πόσις ’husband’) · also πόσις — husband; masc. gen. sg. (εὐνὴν … πόσιος ’her husband’s bed’)
σιγαλόεντα: σιγαλόεις — glossy, gleaming (sense uncertain); neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with χιτῶνα: ’gleaming’
σιδήρεον: σιδήρεος — of iron; masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic σιδηροῦς), agreeing with οὐρανόν
σοὶ: σύ — you (sg.); dat. sg.: ’to, for you’
στήθεσσι: στῆθος — breast, chest; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι
σφισιν: σφεῖς — they; epic dat. pl. pron. (= Attic αὐτοῖς): ’to/for them’
σὴν: σός — your, yours; fem. acc. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’ · also after ἤ ’than’, with no connective force: ἤ τ’ οἰωνοί ’than birds’ · also after ὅ ‘that’, with no connective force: ὅ τ’ οὐκέτι νόστιμός ἐστιν ‘that he is no longer returning’
τέκνον: τέκνον — child; neut. voc. sg. (= nom./acc. in form)
τέχνην: τέχνη — craft, skill, cunning device; fem. acc. sg.
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj. · also plain interrogative, direct object/predicate: ’what’ (τί πάθω ’what am I to suffer’; τί ... γένηται ’what is to become’) · also the enclitic indefinite as an adjective agreeing with a noun, accented before enclitic που: εἴ τί που εἴλυμα ’if any wrapper’ · also enclitic indefinite with a negative, ’anything’, as accusative subject of an infinitive (οὐ … τί φημι κακώτερον ἄλλο … συγχεῦαι ’I say nothing else is worse’) · also enclitic indefinite, adverbial without a negative: ’somehow, in some way’ (τοῦτό τί μοι κάλλιστον ’this seems to me somehow the fairest’) · also enclitic indefinite as an adjective after μή, accented before an enclitic: ’any’ (μή τί τοι … πῆμα ’any harm to you’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ὅπως, accented before enclitic μοι: ’any’ (τί … ἄλγος ’any pain’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ἤ, accented before the enclitic μοι: ’any’ (ἤ τί μοι … κειμήλιον ’or any treasure of mine’) · also the enclitic indefinite as a substantive object after εἴ: ’anything’ (εἴ τί μιν εἴποι ’whether she would say anything to him’)
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
τίφθ: τίπτε (τί ποτε) — why, what then?; interrog. adv., elided τίπτ’, and τίφθ’ before a rough breathing
ταμίη: ταμίη — housekeeper, stewardess, woman with charge of the stores (Attic ταμία, Ionic η for α); nom. sg.
ταῦτά: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’, accented before an enclitic
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τελείει: τελέω (epic τελείω) — bring to completion, accomplish; pres. 3 sg., epic (= Attic τελεῖ)
τετληότι: τλάω — endure, have the heart to bear; perf. part. (τετληώς) masc./neut. dat. sg.: ’enduring’
τηλέμαχ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. voc. sg., elided (Τηλέμαχ’ = Τηλέμαχε)
τηλέμαχον: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. acc. sg.
τηλέμαχος: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; nom. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’) · also ὅ τι as an adverbial acc. in an indirect question: ’why’ · also as a substantive object in a statement: ’something’ (καί τι ἴσασι ’they know something’) · also neut. acc. sg. as object with a negative: ’anything’ (οὐδέ τι ῥέξαι ’nor to have done anything’)
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also with a negative: ’any, anyone’ (οὐ … τις ’no one’; οὐδέ τις ’nor any’) · also after the relative ὅς, indefinite: ὅς τις ’whichever, whoever’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιγὰρ: τοιγάρ — well then, accordingly; particle introducing a response to a request
τοὔνεκ: τοὔνεκα — for that reason, on that account (τοῦ ἕνεκα); adv., elided (τοὔνεκ’)
τοῖσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’from/to them’ · also relative, masc./neut. dat. pl. ’on which’ (κώεα, τοῖσιν ἐνεῦδεν ’the fleeces on which he had slept’) · also masc. dat. pl. after ἐν, ’among them’ (ἐν … τοῖσιν) · also neut. dat. pl., ’with those’, pointing back to a group of things: τοῖσιν Ὀδυσσῆος ’with those of Odysseus’
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whose, of whom; masc. gen. sg. (τοῦ νῶι θεοῦ ὣς τερπόμεθ’ αὐδῇ ’whose voice we delight in’) · also demonstrative gen. of comparison after a comparative: τοῦ γε κρεῖσσον ’better than this’ · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐκ τοῦ: ’from that time’ · also neut. gen. sg., partitive, ’of it’ (τοῦ μὲν ὅσον τ’ ὄργυιαν ’of it, about a fathom’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the’ (τοῦ παιδὸς ’that son’) · also article-like gen. sg. with a noun and a participle (gen. absolute), distributive: ’of the one … of the other’ (τοῦ μὲν φθίνοντος μηνός, τοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένοιο ’as one month wanes and the other begins’)
τόν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg.: ’him’; also relative: ’whom’ · also demonstrative with a noun, ’that’, antecedent of a relative: ἄνδρα τόν, ὅς κε … ’that man who …’ · also masc. acc. sg. ’it’, of a thing (τόν ῥ’ ἐπὶ πήχει ἑλών ’taking it on the bow-grip’, of the arrow)
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’) · also relative, neut. acc. pl.: ’which’, object of the verb in its clause (ῥωγαλέα, τὰ … ὅρηαι ’torn, which you see’) · also article-like with a substantivized adjective, neut.: ’the (worse things)’ (τὰ χέρεια) · also neut. acc. pl. ’them’, of the cow and the goats · also article-like before an adverb, ’the (things) outside’ (τὰ θύρηφι)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον) · also article-like with a substantivized adjective: ’the like (one)’ (τὸν ὁμοῖον)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun · also relative adv., ’where, in the place where’ (τῇ δή μοι ἐείσατο χῶρος ἄριστος) · also adverbial, ’in that (event)’, pointing back to a contest just named: τῇ δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύαλος ἀπεκαίνυτο ’in that Euryalus in turn outdid all’ · also relative adv. of manner, with περ: ’in just the way that’ · also adv. of direction, ’thither, that way’ · also with a noun, article-like: fem. dat. sg. ’the’ (τῇ δεκάτῃ ’on the tenth’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., of respect or means: ’in which, by which’ (ἀγλαΐην, τῇ … κέκασσαι ’the beauty by which you excel’)
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’) · also demonstrative of a thing just named, before a preposition: ’it’ (τῷ δ’ ἐν ’and on it’, τῷ δ’ ὑπό ’and beneath it’) · also adverbial, with κε: ’in that case, otherwise’ (τῷ κέ μιν … παύσαμεν ’otherwise we should have stopped him’)
φάσ: φημί — say, assert; pres. 3 pl., elided (φάσ’ = φασί): ’they say’
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλε: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. voc. sg.
φαίη: φημί — say, assert; pres. opt. 3 sg., with κέν: ’might say’
φημι: φημί — say, declare, assert; pres. 1 sg.
φράζεσθαι: φράζω — point out, tell; mid. φράζομαι consider, think out, devise; pres. inf. mid.: ’to consider’; also used as an imperative: ’consider!’ · also pres. inf. mid. after ἀνώγει: ’to watch, to keep guard on’ (φράζεσθαι ’to keep watch on’)
φραζώμεθ: φράζομαι — think out, devise, plan; pres. subj. 1 pl. mid., hortative, elided (φραζώμεθ’ = φραζώμεθα) ’let us plan’
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φόνου: φόνος — killing, slaughter; masc. gen. sg.
φόρμιγγα: φόρμιγξ — lyre, the singer’s stringed instrument; fem. acc. sg.
φᾶρος: φᾶρος — large cloth, robe, web; neut. acc. sg.
φῶτα: φώς — man, mortal; masc. acc. sg.
χάριν: χάρις — grace, charm; fem. acc. sg.
χαρίεντα: χαρίεις — graceful, lovely; neut. acc. pl.
χεῦεν: χέω — pour; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (contrast augmented ἔχευε)
χλαίνας: χλαῖνα — a thick cloak, mantle; fem. acc. pl.
χροῒ: χρώς — skin, flesh, the body’s surface; dat. sg. χροΐ
ἀγρὸν: ἀγρός — field, farmland, country; masc. acc. sg.
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀθανάτοισιν: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. dat. pl., epic (= Attic -οις)
ἀθερίζω: ἀθερίζω — slight, make light of; pres. 1 sg.
ἀκούων: ἀκούω — hear; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’hearing’
ἀλκῆς: ἀλκή — might, valor, prowess in battle; fem. gen. sg. (θούριδος ἀλκῆς ’furious valor’)
ἀλλήλων: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., gen. pl.
ἀλόχου: ἄλοχος — wife; fem. gen. sg., with πρός · also fem. gen. sg. as object of πειράω (+ gen.): ’of your wife’ (σῆς ἀλόχου πειρήσεαι ’you will make trial of your wife’) · also fem. gen. sg., with ἐκ: ’of a wedded wife’ (ἐξ ἀλόχου ’by a wife’)
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀμφὶ ... βάλλομεν = ἀμφιβάλλομεν ’we threw around, embraced’)
ἀμύμονος: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (an old epithet whose exact force is uncertain); gen. sg.
ἀν: ἀνά (elided ἀν’) — up, along; prep. + acc.: ἀν’ ἰθύν ’in a straight line’ · also + acc., ’throughout, up and down’ (ἀν’ Ἑλλάδα ’throughout Hellas’)
ἀνέστη: ἀνίστημι — stand up, rise; aor. 3 sg. intrans.: ’stood up’
ἀνείρεαι: ἀνείρομαι — ask, inquire; pres. 2 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic -ῃ)
ἀνθρώπους: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; acc. pl.

ἀοσσητῆρες: ἀοσσητήρ — helper, defender; masc. nom. pl.

ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀπηνέα: ἀπηνής — unkind, harsh, unfeeling; neut. acc. pl., substantival, uncontracted (= Attic ἀπηνῆ): ’unkind things’
ἀτιμάζει: ἀτιμάζω — dishonour, slight, scorn; pres. 3 sg.

ἄλλος: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. sg.
ἄλοχον: ἄλοχος — wife, one who shares the bed; acc. sg.
ἄνθει: ἄνθος — flower, blossom; neut. dat. sg.
ἄνωγα: ἄνωγα — bid, command, order; perf. 1 sg. with pres. sense: ’I bid’
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel · also the shortened form ἄρ used, without true elision, before τε in the fixed collocation ἄρ τε: τὰ μὲν ἄρ τε διεσκέδασ’ · also ἄρ before an elided κ’ (κε), ’then’, in a question: ἦ ἄρ κ’ ἐθέλοις ’would you then be willing?’ · also the shortened ἄρ before a consonant, without elision: ’then’ (ἐπεὶ ἄρ βλέφαρ’ … ἀμφικαλύψῃ ’when then (sleep) has covered the eyelids’) · also ἄρ before ἕζετ’ without elision: ’then’ (κατ’ ἄρ ἕζετ’ ’then sat down’)
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄρειον: ἀρείων — better, more excellent; neut. nom. sg., comparative
ἄριστα: ἀγαθός (superl. ἄριστος) — best; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’best’ (ὄχ’ ἄριστα ’far the best’)
ἄριστοι: ἄριστος — best; superl., masc. nom. pl.
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐεικοστῷ: εἰκοστός — twentieth; epic ἐεικοστός (prothetic ε-), masc./neut. dat. sg.
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐλαίῳ: ἔλαιον — olive oil; neut. dat. sg.
ἐλθέμεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. inf., epic ἐλθέμεν (= Attic ἐλθεῖν): ’to come’
ἐμέθεν: ἐγώ — I; epic gen. sg. ἐμέθεν (= Attic ἐμοῦ): ’of me’
ἐμή: ἐμός — my, mine; fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg. (= nom. in form), agreeing with μῆτερ: ’my (mother)’

ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)

ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)

ἐπίθοντο: πείθω — persuade; mid. obey; aor. mid. 3 pl., augmented (unaugmented πίθοντο): ’they obeyed’
ἐποίει: ποιέω — make, produce, do; impf. 3 sg., augmented: ’was making, gave’
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’ · also + acc. of time: ’for, over’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + dat., ’in charge of, over’ (ἐπὶ κτεάτεσσιν ’over my possessions’) · also + dat., of purpose: ’for’ (ἐπὶ δόρπῳ ’for supper’) · also + dat., of the occasion: ’at, over’ (ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ ’at a fair remark’)
ἐρέεσθαι: ἐρέομαι — ask, inquire; pres. inf., epic (= Attic ἐρέσθαι): ’to ask’
ἐρέω: ἐρέω — say, tell, declare; fut. 1 sg. (epic fut. of εἶπον, = Attic ἐρῶ); in tmesis with ἐκ, ἐξερέω ’speak out plainly’
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐτέτυκτο: τεύχω — make, contrive, bring about; pass. come to pass, happen; plup. pass. 3 sg. with impf. sense: ’had been wrought, had come about’
ἐτεὸν: ἐτεός — true, real; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’truly, in truth’
ἐϋσταθέος: ἐϋσταθής — well-standing, firmly built; masc./neut. gen. sg., epic uncontracted -έος (= Attic -οῦς)
ἑζομένη: ἕζομαι — seat oneself, sit down; pres. part. mid. fem. nom. sg.: ’sitting down’
ἑλέσθαι: αἱρέω — take, take up; aor. mid. inf.: ’to take (for oneself)’
ἔγημε: γαμέω — marry (of a man), take as wife; aor. 3 sg., augmented (ἔ-γημε): ’married’
ἔειπε: εἶπον — say, speak, tell; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept before the root’s own ει- (= Attic εἶπε)
ἔησθα: εἰμί — be; impf. 2 sg., epic ἔησθα (= Attic ἦσθα): ’you were’
ἔθηκαν: τίθημι — put, place, set; aor. 3 pl., built like the sg. ἔθηκε rather than the root-aorist (= Attic ἔθεσαν)
ἔλθοι: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. opt. 3 sg. ἔμμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’) · also doubled, ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’this way and that’
ἔνθεν: ἔνθεν — from there, thence; adv. of place, with suffix -θεν · also ’on the one side’ (ἔνθεν μὲν γὰρ πέτραι ’on one side are rocks’) · also relative, ’from which, whence’ (ἔνθεν ἔπινον ’from which they drank’)
ἔπεα: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἔπη)
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔστ: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., elided (ἔστ’ = ἔστι)
ἔστι: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg. impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also existential, ‘there is’ (ἔστι δέ τις πέτρη ‘there is a rock’)
ἔτεϊ: ἔτος — year; neut. dat. sg., epic (= Attic ἔτει)
ἔτλη: τλάω — bring oneself to, dare, endure; aor. 3 sg. (ἔτλην, inf. τλῆναι)

ἔχων: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’holding’
ἔωσιν: εἰμί — be; pres. subj. 3 pl., epic ἔωσιν (= Attic ὦσιν)
ἕζετ: ἕζομαι — sit down; impf. 3 sg., elided (ἕζετ’ = ἕζετο), in tmesis with κατά: ’sat down’ · also plain, no tmesis: ’sat’ (ἕζετ’ ἔπειτ’ ἐπὶ θῖνα ’then sat down on the shore’)
ἕνα: εἷς, μία, ἕν — one; masc. acc. sg. (ἕνα θυμόν ’one mind’)
ἡμέας: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; acc. pl., epic ἡμέας (= Attic ἡμᾶς)
ἡμέτερον: ἡμέτερος — our, ours; neut. acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with κάματον: ’our (toil)’
ἡμεῖς: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; nom. pl. ’we’

ἥφαιστος: Ἥφαιστος — Hephaestus, god of the forge; nom. sg.

ἧκε: ἵημι — send, let go, let fall; aor. 3 sg. (with κὰδ in tmesis: ’let down’) · also of hurling a missile: ’hurled’ (ἧκε … κορυφὴν ὄρεος ’hurled the peak of a mountain’) · also with ἐν in tmesis: ’put in’ (ἐν … ἧκε) · also with ὑπό in tmesis: ’set beneath’ (ὑπὸ θρῆνυν … ἧκε ’set a footstool beneath’) · also with πρό in tmesis: ’sent forth’ (πρὸ … ἧκε)

ἧς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. gen. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whose, of whom/which (fem. gen. sg.)
ἰδέσθαι: ὁράω — see; aor. mid. inf.: ‘to see’
ἰὼν: εἶμι — go; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’going’
ἱκάνεται: ἱκάνω — come to, arrive at, reach; pres. 3 sg. mid. (deponent), epic (= Attic ἀφικνεῖται)
ἴδμεν: οἶδα — know; pres. 1 pl., epic ἴδμεν (= Attic ἴσμεν): ’we know’
ἴδρις: ἴδρις — knowing, skilled; masc. nom. sg.
ἴσαν: εἶμι — go, come; impf. 3 pl., epic: ’used to go, come’ · also as a simple narrative past, ’went’ (μνηστῆρες … ἴσαν ’the suitors went’), not necessarily iterative · also οἶδα — know; unaugmented plup. 3 pl. with impf. sense, epic (= Attic ᾔδεσαν): ’they knew’ (τὰ δ’ οὐκ ἴσαν ’they did not know’)
ἵκοιτο: ἱκνέομαι — come to, arrive at, reach; aor. opt. 3 sg. mid., wish/potential: ’might come, may he reach’
ἵμερον: ἵμερος — longing, desire, yearning; masc. acc. sg.
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. acc. sg., double-σ form (metrical variant of Ὀδυσῆα)
ὀλύμπια: Ὀλύμπιος — Olympian, of Olympus; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ὀλύμπιος: Ὀλύμπιος — Olympian, of Olympus; adj., masc. nom. sg. (epithet of Zeus)
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv. · also ’back, home again’, of return (οἴκαδ’ ὀπίσσω ’back home’)
ὀρχηθμοῖο: ὀρχηθμός — dancing, dance; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ὀχθήσας: ὀχθέω — be vexed, be troubled; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’vexed, troubled’
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’) · also article-like with a superlative: ’the worst’ (ὁ κάκιστος Ἀχαιῶν ’the worst of the Achaeans’)
ὁδὸν: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὁμοίας: ὅμοιος — like, similar; fem. acc. pl., + dat.: ’like’
ὁμοῖος: ὅμοιος — like, similar; masc. nom. sg., + dat.
ὃν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (masc. acc. sg.)
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. ὄχ: ὄχα — by far, exceedingly; adv., elided (ὄχ’ = ὄχα), intensifying a superlative (ὄχ’ ἄριστα ’far the best’)
ὅπως: ὅπως — so that, in order that, how; + subj. or fut. indic. · also + opt., in secondary sequence after a past-tense verb, indirect deliberative: ’how it might’ (ὅπως ἄριστα γένοιτο ’how it might turn out best’) · also ’when’ = ὅτε · also ’as, however’ + subj. in a general clause: ὅπως ἐθέλῃσιν ’however he wishes’ · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a past tense: ’so that … might follow’ (ὅπως … ἑποίατο) · also + pres. indic., ’as, in whatever way’ (ὅπως ἐθέλεις ’as you wish’) · also ’how’ + aor. indic., indirect question after a verb of telling (κατάλεξον ὅπως ἤντησας ’tell how you came upon’)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὅση: ὅσος — as great as, as much as; relative adj., fem. nom. sg., of measure
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’) · also in ὅτε μή, ’unless, except when’ (ὅτε μὴ θεὸς … θείη ’unless a god should make’)
ὅττι: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; epic neut. nom./acc. sg. ὅττι (= Attic ὅ τι) · also with a superlative, ’as … as possible’ (ὅττι τάχιστα ’as quickly as possible’) · also in an indirect question, ’what’ (ὅττι ἑ κήδοι ’what was troubling him’) · also conj. ’that, because’, introducing a clause (ὅττι μιν ὣς ὑπέδεκτο ’that he had received him so’)
ὑακινθίνῳ: ὑακίνθινος — of hyacinth; neut. dat. sg.
